question: Is `ProviderInteractionContext.userInitiated` an approved trust boundary for allowing a Grok browser-cookie import, including every current and future caller that can set it?
rationale: The code changes when CodexBar may access browser-held authentication material; source and focused tests show the intended CLI refresh behavior, but maintainers must decide whether the context’s broader semantic contract is an acceptable authorization boundary.

options.title: Approve the explicit-action boundary
options.body: Treat the existing user-initiated context as the approved boundary and merge after current-head stale-team proof is added.

options.title: Narrow the gate to cookie refresh
options.body: Pass a refresh-specific capability through the CLI refresh path if the generic interaction context may be set by flows that should not access browser cookies.

recommendation.title: Approve the explicit-action boundary
recommendation.body: Treat the existing user-initiated context as the approved boundary and merge after current-head stale-team proof is added.

likelyOwner.reason: As repository owner, this person is the best available decision route for the browser-cookie access boundary.
